description.narrative: The ocean is under escalating pressures mainly due to human activities. An ocean literate society is better equipped to take responsible actions for ocean sustainability. Journalists and media professionals, as key intermediaries between ocean and society, play a pivotal role in translating complex ocean issues into accessible, relatable narratives. Their work of accurate, evidence-based reporting shapes public discourse, raises awareness, fosters ocean stewardship, and supports sound policymaking and conservation efforts. For the Western Pacific region, ocean literacy is especially crucial for the countries characterized by rich marine biodiversity, diverse cultural-socio-economic contexts, and high vulnerability to climate change. This project, supported by JIFT, aims to enhance ocean literacy of journalists or media professionals in four pilot countries in the Western Pacific region. It seeks to improve their understandings of ocean, ocean science and its societal relevance, foster collaborative networks between journalists/media groups and ocean experts/institutions, provide journalists with hands-on exposure and practical field experience, and eventually supporting the sustainable development of the ocean.
